```bash
# Date Format Specification

## Accepted Input Date Patterns
- YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2023-05-01, 2023-5-1)

## Supported Format Tokens
- %Y: 4-digit year (e.g., 2023)
- %y: 2-digit year (e.g., 23)
- %m: 2-digit month with zero padding (e.g., 05)
- %d: 2-digit day with zero padding (e.g., 01)
- %B: Full month name (e.g., January)
- %b: Abbreviated month name (e.g., Jan)

## Normalization Rules
- Single-digit months and days are zero-padded when using %m and %d tokens
- Input separators (-, /) are replaced with format-specified separators
- Month and day values are validated (1-12 for months, 1-31 for days)
- Year values must be 4-digit positive integers

## Error Semantics
- Invalid date formats return error message "Invalid date format"
- Invalid month values (< 1 or > 12) return "Invalid month"
- Invalid day values (< 1 or > 31) return "Invalid day"
- Invalid format tokens return "Invalid format token"
- Empty input returns "Empty input not allowed"
EOF
```

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Parse input date and extract components
parse_date() {
    local input="$1"
    local year month day
    
    if [[ -z "$input" ]]; then
        echo "Empty input not allowed"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY/MM/DD
    if [[ "$input" =~ ^([0-9]{4})[-/]([0-9]{1,2})[-/]([0-9]{1,2})$ ]]; then
        year="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        month="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        day="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
    # MM-DD-YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY
    elif [[ "$input" =~ ^([0-9]{1,2})[-/]([0-9]{1,2})[-/]([0-9]{4})$ ]]; then
        month="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        day="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        year="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
    else
        echo "Invalid date format"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo "$year $month $day"
}

# Validate date components
validate_date() {
    local year="$1" month="$2" day="$3"
    
    if [[ $month -lt 1 || $month -gt 12 ]]; then
        echo "Invalid month"
        return 1
    fi
    
    if [[ $day -lt 1 || $day -gt 31 ]]; then
        echo "Invalid day"
        return 1
    fi
    
    return 0
}

# Format date according to format string
format_date() {
    local year="$1" month="$2" day="$3" format="$4"
    local months=("" "January" "February" "March" "April" "May" "June" "July" "August" "September" "October" "November" "December")
    local short_months=("" "Jan" "Feb" "Mar" "Apr" "May" "Jun" "Jul" "Aug" "Sep" "Oct" "Nov" "Dec")
    
    # Normalize components
    local padded_month=$(printf "%02d" $month)
    local padded_day=$(printf "%02d" $day)
    local short_year=$(printf "%02d" $((year % 100)))
    
    # Replace format tokens
    format="${format//%Y/$year}"
    format="${format//%y/$short_year}"
    format="${format//%m/$padded_month}"
    format="${format//%d/$padded_day}"
    format="${format//%B/${months[$month]}}"
    format="${format//%b/${short_months[$month]}}"
    
    echo "$format"
}

# Main function
format_date_main() {
    local input="$1" format="$2"
    
    if [[ -z "$format" ]]; then
        format="%Y-%m-%d"
    fi
    
    local parsed
    parsed=$(parse_date "$input")
    if [[ $? -ne 0 ]]; then
        echo "$parsed"
        return 1
    fi
    
    read -r year month day <<< "$parsed"
    
    if ! validate_date "$year" "$month" "$day"; then
        return 1
    fi
    
    format_date "$year" "$month" "$day" "$format"
}
EOF
```
